titulo: Ask the question whose answer fits in your head
subtitulo: Does one exist, where is the known place, and what to do when the answer becomes a paragraph
cena: A stranger on the corner is already drawing a map in the air with both hands, three streets deep, and you haven't decided yet whether you even need all of it.
frasePiso: The best direction question is the one that gives you a usable next move.

contagem: a pharmacy that may or may not exist
clique.desconto: Nobody handed you four separate direction questions. You built the ladder yourself, out of two openings, by deciding each time how much answer you actually needed.
clique.piso: Next time a local starts drawing a route in the air, you won't try to hold the whole paragraph in your head. You'll cut it down to a decision before it gets away from you.

steps.pt: A stranger might answer with three streets and a hand wave. Start smaller — hay just asks yes or no, and that fits in your head.
Is there a pharmacy around here?

steps.promptPt: You need medicine but do not know whether this street has a pharmacy. Ask the yes-or-no existence question first. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is there a pharmacy around here?

steps.es: Sí, hay una en la esquina.
steps.pt: Yes, there is one on the corner.
steps.tts: Sí, hay una en la esquina.

steps.pt: The frame stays, the thing changes — any cash machine will do. Keep hay, swap only the object.

steps.promptPt: You need any cash machine nearby. Keep the existence opening and replace the object. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is there an ATM around here?
Now the defined place: this café has one bathroom, you're not asking if bathrooms exist. Dónde está finds the known place.
Where is the bathroom?

steps.promptPt: In a café, ask where the bathroom is. It is the known place inside this building. Speak now.
steps.pt: Where is the bathroom?
At the back, on the right.
Dónde hay combines both jobs — the location of any useful instance. Any nearby pharmacy solves the problem.

steps.promptPt: The person confirmed that pharmacies exist nearby. Now ask where you can find one. Speak now.
steps.pt: Where is there a pharmacy?

steps.es: Siga derecho, cruce la avenida y dé vuelta después del mercado.
steps.pt: Go straight, cross the avenue and turn after the market.
steps.tts: Siga derecho, cruce la avenida y dé vuelta después del mercado.

steps.pt: Too large an answer? Don't ask again — collapse it into distance. Near, follow the arm; far, move to the map.

steps.promptPt: The stranger gives you three movements and you lose the middle. Ask only whether it is far. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is it far?
No. It is two blocks away.

steps.promptPt: Two blocks still leaves you unsure which turn begins the route. Open the map and ask the person to show you. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: meh loh MWEHS-trah en el MAH-pah
steps.pt: Can you show me on the map?

steps.es: Sí. Es aquí, en esta esquina.
steps.pt: Yes. It is here, on this corner.
steps.tts: Sí. Es aquí, en esta esquina.

steps.promptPt: Keep the frame, change the thing. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is there a supermarket around here?

steps.promptPt: Simplest possible existence question. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is there water to buy?

steps.promptPt: A known, single place. Use the definite frame. Speak now.
steps.pt: Where is the station?

steps.promptPt: The route they described sounds long. Ask if another exists. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is there another way?

steps.es: ¿Hay una farmacia por aquí? ¿Dónde hay una farmacia? ¿Está lejos?
steps.pinyin: eye OO-nah fahr-MAH-syah por ah-KEE. DOHN-deh eye OO-nah fahr-MAH-syah. ehs-TAH LEH-hohs
steps.pt: Shadow the ladder from existence to location to distance.
steps.tts: ¿Hay una farmacia por aquí? ¿Dónde hay una farmacia? ¿Está lejos?

steps.pt: B08 complete. Hay for exists, dónde está for the known place, dónde hay for any instance, está lejos to collapse it all.

secoes.corpo: Use ¿Hay…? when yes or no is already valuable. Keep the opening and replace the object.

exemplos.pt: Is there a pharmacy around here?
Is there an ATM around here?

secoes.corpo: Use ¿Dónde está el baño? for the bathroom in this building. Use ¿Dónde hay una farmacia? when any nearby pharmacy will do.
Direction words are mainly receptive here: derecho, esquina, cuadra, derecha. Your production job is to reduce the answer with ¿Está lejos? or move it onto the map.
B03 already taught the visual repair. B08 makes it part of direction-finding, so the learner never has to perform complete comprehension before moving.

permissao: You are allowed to cut a stranger's answer short. Asking ¿Está lejos? or pulling out the map before someone finishes a three-street explanation is not impatience — it is the fastest way to end up somewhere useful instead of nodding through directions you were never going to retain.
espelho: Anyone who has ever asked a local for directions back home and immediately lost the thread after 'turn left at the second light' has already lived the failure mode B08 is solving — the instinct to keep nodding rather than interrupt a stranger mid-explanation is universal, not a Spanish-specific problem.

fichasCulturais.sinal: A stranger answers your direction question with a long string of turns and landmarks, and you catch the first two words and lose the rest.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: I should have understood all of that, or asking again will seem rude.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: A full spoken route is a lot of information to hold in your head in any language, and Mexican direction-giving culture tends to be generous and detailed rather than terse — the generosity is real, but it produces more than a first-time visitor can retain in one pass.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Reduce the answer instead of asking for it again in full: ask ¿Está lejos? for a near/far decision, or open the map and ask them to show you the point.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You leave with one usable fact — near, far, or a pin on a map — instead of a paragraph you cannot reconstruct two turns later.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not when someone has already reduced the answer for you unprompted (e.g. 'it's right there') — in that case a follow-up question would ask for detail that was never missing.
